## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Quarterly baseline to local Parquet
      Objective: Fetch a configured range of real archived quarterly master indexes and turn them into a Parquet filing-index dataset on a single machine.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing (the package scaffolds only)
      Produces: raw quarterly snapshots kept as original bytes with SHA-256; a quarterly parser and the §4.5 row contract (`sec-index-v1`); the Parquet dataset; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — every quarter in the configured range is downloaded with an identifying User-Agent at ≤3 req/s, and failed quarters are reported as such. O3 — a Parquet dataset meeting the §4.5 row contract is built from those snapshots, with malformed rows refused. Cost — elapsed time, request count and rate, bytes downloaded, row count and peak memory of the real run are recorded in the findings file.
      Leaves out: daily sources (Stage 2); versioned processing identities and replay without SEC access (Stage 3); manifests, generations and the active pointer (Stage 3); reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 4); Azure and the shared lease (Stage 5); full §6 validation suite, observability, runbooks and schedules (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion on the shared code
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from a handoff date, through the same downloader and parser as Stage 1.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader, raw snapshot store, parser and row contract
      Produces: daily discovery with per-source pending and failed state; daily observations in the Stage 1 dataset; one code path for every source kind
      Exit: O2 — a run after missed days ingests every listed unprocessed daily file, across a quarter boundary, reporting `no_new_sources` and unresolved gaps distinctly. O5 — quarterly and daily sources run through one downloader and one parser, with no kind-specific copy.
      Leaves out: replay and versioned publication (Stage 3); Azure, scheduling and the shared lease (Stages 5–6); full §6 validation suite (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Replay and versioned publication
      Objective: Reprocess stored snapshots without the SEC and publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind one conditional pointer.
      Outcomes: O6, O9
      Consumes: Stages 1–2's raw snapshots, parser and observations
      Produces: the §4.5 source manifest (source, snapshot, processing and attempt records); per-quarter generations with manifest.json and changes.parquet; the active-pointer reader contract
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds output from stored bytes with zero SEC requests and no duplicate logical records. O9 — readers resolve each quarter through its pointer, and a crash injected before or after the pointer update leaves only a complete generation readable.
      Leaves out: reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 4); Azure Table Storage and ADLS as the backing stores (Stage 5); full §6 validation suite (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Reconciliation and gated withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and apply the §4.4 precedence, change and withdrawal rules through Stage 3's publication path.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 3's manifest, generations, changes report and pointer
      Produces: a reconciliation command; hash-bound withdrawal approval records; the `awaiting_approval` generation state
      Exit: O7 — a changed quarterly snapshot publishes its additions and field updates, and unchanged bytes skip transformation. O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays unpublished until an approval names its source hash, and open-quarter absence withdraws nothing.
      Leaves out: Azure and the shared lease (Stage 5); the weekly schedule and approval runbook (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Azure platform and one request budget
      Objective: Run the shared commands on the R4 platform, with every SEC collector under one Storage-backed lease.
      Outcomes: O4, O8
      Consumes: Stages 1–4's commands; the ADR accepted (currently Proposed)
      Produces: versioned infrastructure, managed identities, the container image and ADF pipelines in an isolated environment; the shared lease
      Exit: O4 — ADF starts, polls and judges a Container Apps job by its worker result file in the isolated environment, with ambiguous starts never relaunched. O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors issue requests from one budget, and lease loss stops requests.
      Leaves out: production schedules, alerts and runbooks (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Configuration review, hardening and scheduled operation
      Objective: Validate configuration before I/O, complete the §6 suite, and move to scheduled production per §7.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 5's deployed environment
      Produces: typed configuration with the §4.8 defaults; the full §6 CI suite; alerts and reports per §4.7; runbooks per §8; enabled triggers
      Exit: O11 — every §5 configuration error is refused before external I/O, and the §4.8 values are the running defaults. Scheduled operation — the §7 exit list holds, including observed scheduled runs recorded apart from the smoke-test results.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans
